sentences.text:
Author: B. Vijaysen Reddy
Bench: B. Vijaysen Reddy
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice B. Vijaysen Reddy
 Writ Petition No.6274 of 2023
Order:
This Writ Petition is filed declaring the action of the respondent Nos.2 to 4 in not acting on the complaint of the petitioner dated 21.1.2023 as arbitrary and illegal.

2. The learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home, having received written instructions dated 9.3.2023 from the Sub-Inspector of Police, Jawaharnagar Police Station, Rachakonda Commissionerate, submitted that the petitioner sent complaint dated 21.1.2023 to the Commissioner of Police, Rachakonda Commissionerate stating that one Vaddicherla Sudarshan, S/o Narsaiah offered to sell Plot No.37 admeasuring 293 sq.yards in Sy.Nos.83, 84, 85, 93 part, 99 and 100 situated at Yapral, Alwal to the petitioner under agreement of sale dated 11.8.2021 for a sale consideration of Rs.47,18,000/- and petitioner paid Rs.35,00,000/-, but later he came to know that he was cheated by the said Sudarshan.
Petitioner filed suit for specific performance vide O.S.No.652 of 2022 on the file of Senior Civil Judge, Malkajgiri and the same is pending.

On the complaint lodged by one Vadaka Sridhar, who was also one of the victim of the said Sudarshan, Crime No.121 of 2022 was registered under Sections 406, 420 and 506 of IPC on the file of Neredmet Police Station.
3. The learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home submitted that since the suit filed by the petitioner is pending, he was advised to approach the concerned Court for redressal of his grievance.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted as the petitioner sustained loss of Rs.35,00,000/-, the Police ought to have registered his complaint and ought to have taken up the matter for investigation.

5. This Court is of the view that closure of petitioner's complaint on the ground that investigation was completed and charge sheet was filed in a similar complaint i.e. Crime No.121 of 2022 is unsustainable.

4. In view of the above, the writ petition is disposed of, granting liberty to the petitioner to lodge fresh complaint as per the provisions of Cr.P.C. and on receipt of such complaint, the respondent No.3 shall conduct enquiry/investigation by following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Lalitha Kumari v. State of Uttar Pradesh1 and shall file final report within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
